title: Realization of a finite graded module on the affine base change
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings and B an A-algebra. Let graded_m be A-submodules of B giving an internal direct sum decomposition indexed by natural numbers, with 1 in graded_0, graded_k * graded_l contained in graded_(k+l), and every algebraMap(a) in graded_0. Let X be a scheme, f : X → Spec(A), and G_m quasi-coherent O_X-modules. Suppose mu m k b : G_m → G_(m+k) is O_X-linear for b in graded_k, additive in b, satisfies mu m l b' followed by mu (m+l) k b = mu m (k+l) (b*b') after the degree associativity identification, and mu m 0 (algebraMap(a)) acts on sections by multiplication by the restriction of f-sharp(a). Suppose each point x has an open neighbourhood U, finitely many degrees d_i and sections s_i of G_(d_i)(U), such that every section t of G_m(V), V contained in U, is locally at each point of V in the O_X-span of mu (d_i) (m-d_i) b applied to the restriction of s_i, with d_i ≤ m and b in graded_(m-d_i), with the canonical degree identification. Set b = Spec(A → B), Y = X ×_Spec(A) Spec(B), and pi = Y → X. Then there exists a quasi-coherent O_Y-module F of finite type together with an O_X-linear isomorphism pi_*F ≅ direct sum_m G_m. No properness, Noetherianity, finite-type-algebra, ampleness or cohomology assumption is made.

proof.text: Let b = Spec(A → B), Y = X ×_Spec(A) Spec(B), and pi = Y → X. Morphisms between affine schemes are affine and affineness is stable under base change. On an affine open U = Spec(R) of X, pi inverse U is Spec(R tensor_A B). The associated-module and tensor-pullback descriptions, equivalently relative Spec base change, identify pi_*O_Y with f^*B~.

proof.text: Let M be the sheaf coproduct of G_m; it is quasi-coherent. Define the action of a homogeneous b in B_k on G_m by mu m k b followed by the coproduct inclusion of G_(m+k). Extend over the internal direct sum decomposition of B and the coproduct universal property of M. hmu_add gives additivity in b, hmu_mul gives associativity, and hmu_scalar identifies the A-action with the structural A-action and gives the unit law at a=1. These actions commute with O_X-scalars because each mu is a module-sheaf morphism. On affine U = Spec(R), the resulting B-action extends to an R tensor_A B-action. This description commutes with restriction and localization, so glues to a module N over pi_*O_Y with underlying O_X-module M. The first clause of affine_module_correspondence implies N is quasi-coherent as a pi_*O_Y-module.

proof.text: Near each x choose U, r, d_i and s_i from hfinite. Regard s_i as sections of M via the coproduct inclusions. A section of the sheaf coproduct is locally represented by a finite sum of homogeneous sections: the coproduct is the sheafification of the presheaf direct sum. At any point, apply hfinite to these finitely many sections and intersect the resulting open neighbourhoods. Each restricted homogeneous section lies in the stated span of mu_b(s_i). A span element is a finite sum of O_X-coefficient multiples of these expressions; these are pi_*O_Y-coefficients times s_i by the algebra action constructed above. Thus the s_i generate N locally as a pi_*O_Y-module; the evaluation map from the finite free algebra module is locally surjective, hence epi. This is N.IsFiniteType.

proof.text: Apply the inverse in affine_module_correspondence to N to get a quasi-coherent O_Y-module F and an algebra-linear pushforward isomorphism. Apply affine_module_finite_type to N, F and that isomorphism to obtain F.IsFiniteType. Restrict the algebra-linear isomorphism to O_X to get (pushforward pi).obj F ≅ M. This yields the existential conclusion. These are witnesses in a theorem, not arbitrary data selected in a definition.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_graded_module_affine_baseChange
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (graded : ℕ → Submodule A B)
    (hgrading : DirectSum.IsInternal graded)
    (hunit : (1 : B) ∈ graded 0)
    (hmul : ∀ (k l : ℕ) {x y : B}, x ∈ graded k → y ∈ graded l → x * y ∈ graded (k + l))
    (hscalar : ∀ (a : A), algebraMap A B a ∈ graded 0)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (G : ℕ → X.Modules)
    (hG : ∀ m : ℕ, (G m).IsQuasicoherent)
    (mu : ∀ (m k : ℕ), graded k → (G m ⟶ G (m + k)))
    (hmu_add : ∀ (m k : ℕ) (b b' : graded k),
      mu m k (b + b') = mu m k b + mu m k b')
    (hmu_mul : ∀ (m k l : ℕ) (b : graded k) (b' : graded l),
      HEq (mu m l b' ≫ mu (m + l) k b)
        (mu m (k + l) ⟨b.val * b'.val, hmul k l b.property b'.property⟩))
    (hmu_scalar : ∀ (m : ℕ) (a : A) (U : X.Opens)
      (t : (G m).val.obj (op U)),
      HEq ((mu m 0 ⟨algebraMap A B a, hscalar a⟩).val.app (op U) t)
        ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top (a := U))).op).hom
          (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom a) • t))
    (hfinite : ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens), x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ (r : ℕ) (d : Fin r → ℕ) (s : ∀ i : Fin r, (G (d i)).val.obj (op U)),
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U) (t : (G m).val.obj (op V))
          (y : X), y ∈ V → ∃ (W : X.Opens) (hWV : W ≤ V), y ∈ W ∧
            (G m).val.map (homOfLE hWV).op t ∈
              Submodule.span ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op W))
                {z | ∃ (i : Fin r), d i ≤ m ∧
                  ∃ b : graded (m - d i),
                    HEq z ((mu (d i) (m - d i) b).val.app (op W)
                      ((G (d i)).val.map (homOfLE (hWV.trans hVU)).op (s i)))}) :
    let b : Spec (.of B) ⟶ Spec (.of A) := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))
    ∃ F : (pullback f b).Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent ∧ F.IsFiniteType ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.fst f b)).obj F ≅ ∐ G)
